plays.story: Binance's $6.3B hack tied to North Korea's TraderTraitor group is rattling crypto markets (BTC near $77K, BNB down 8%, RUNE up 13%) while security researchers dissect how the breach happened.

angles.itsalreadypriced: Title: 'The Market Already Called It: BNB Down 8%, RUNE Up 13% — Pricing the $6.3B Binance Hack in Real Time.' Track the divergent price reactions (BNB crash vs RUNE pump vs BTC flight-to-safety) as a live case study in how markets price catastrophic exchange risk before the postmortem even lands.
angles.itsalreadywhen: Title: 'TraderTraitor Strikes Again: Why Binance's $6.3B Breach Was Always a Matter of When, Not If.' Frame North Korea's repeat playbook (laptop compromise, EIP-7702 amplification) as the predictable next chapter in a threat actor's well-documented timeline — not a surprise.

plays.story: A supply-chain attack drained $2.65M from Polymarket users via a compromised third-party provider, echoing the same GitHub-issues supply-chain campaign that hit 61 public repos within an hour.

angles.itsalreadypriced: Title: 'Prediction Markets Pay a Hack Tax: What Polymarket's $2.65M Breach Prices Into Betting on Trustless Platforms.' Analyze how the exploit changes risk premiums and confidence pricing for prediction-market tokens going into year-end.
angles.itsalreadywhen: Title: 'It's Already When: The Same Supply-Chain Playbook That Drained Polymarket Just Hit 61 GitHub Repos in Under an Hour.' Connect the dots between the GitHub issues campaign and the Polymarket breach to show attackers reusing a known technique faster than defenders can patch it.

plays.story: The One Ring's designer is building a Clive Barker Hellraiser TTRPG.

angles.bizzal-games: Title: 'Pinhead Rolls Initiative: What a Hellraiser TTRPG From The One Ring's Designer Could Actually Play Like.' Speculate on mechanics — pain/pleasure dice pools, Cenobite bargains, horror-survival loops — drawing on the designer's known system for Middle-earth.
angles.itsalreadywritten: Title: 'The Box Was Always Going to Open: Hellraiser's TTRPG Adaptation Was Written Into the Cenobites' Rules All Along.' Frame the licensing deal as inevitable lore convergence — horror fiction's obsession with rules, contracts, and 'rules lawyers from Hell' finally formalized into an actual rulebook.
